issues.where: data/public/tasks/pub-nih-ruralbp-close/task.yaml, T1 expected_behaviour: "Develop and assess the workflow through formative co-design and structured usability tasks using simulated cases".
issues.problem: The clinical-trial trap is sound, but the key makes simulated cases mandatory. The call requires structured usability evidence, not a particular source of test cases. A non-therapeutic usability study using appropriately governed existing/de-identified records, or observational workflow assessment without assigned care, can satisfy it. A valid proposal could therefore fail the trap solely for choosing another compliant method.
issues.fix: Replace the prescriptive sentence with 'Develop and assess the workflow using a feasible formative or methodological design that does not prospectively assign care to evaluate a health-related effect; simulated-case usability testing is one option, not a requirement. Accept other appropriately governed non-clinical-trial usability or observational workflow designs. In Specific Aims and Approach, keep any therapeutic controlled evaluation as a future study outside this award.' Retain the prohibition on the brief's randomized BP-effect pilot.

issues.where: data/public/tasks/pub-nih-ruralbp-close/brief.md: the opening notes have no date.
issues.problem: The revised checklist requires briefs dated 1 October 2026. The task-wide present date makes this omission recoverable, so it is polish rather than an undecidable trap.

checked: Task 1, 3: strong close fit to adult rural BP measurement, record linkage, interviews and paper-workflow experience. Existing clinic relationships do not guarantee new staff time, record access or recruitment; the brief preserves that distinction.

Task 2, 6: T1 is correctly T05. Randomizing the 60 adults to a follow-up workflow/usual care and evaluating six-month systolic BP is a clinical trial even if labelled a pilot. T2 is correctly T02: the requested third award year contradicts the explicit 24-month cap.

Task 2, 6: T2 expected behaviour correctly permits any ≤24-month schedule covering the call outcomes and excludes only award work after month 24; it does not forbid describing a separately funded later evaluation. The two planted mistakes can be corrected together by moving empirical/formative work into a two-year schedule.

Task 1: a 60-adult, two-clinic measurement/linkage study plus bounded co-design and usability work can meet all outcomes within an R21; no definitive treatment effect or new intervention evidence is required. Six hundred Aims words and 3,600 Strategy words are adequate.

Task 4, 5, 7: ordinary English applicant notes, two keyed traps, full new application. No silent/reviewer-criticism/ethics trap; RESUB does not apply. The duplicated call exclusion and historical-analysis issue are filed on the call/dossier, not repeated here.
